name: Renaissance and Early Tudor Period
description: The literature of England (with a significant Scottish companion tradition) from the turn of the sixteenth century to the accession of Elizabeth I: the flowering of Erasmian humanism under the early Tudors, the court poetry of Skelton, Wyatt, and Surrey, the first English comedies and interludes, the chronicles and biographies of the new nation-state, and the polemical, liturgical, and scriptural writing of the English Reformation.
